html:
The destruction of Sybaris, a Greek city on the Gulf of Taranto in southern Italy, by its neighbour Croton in 510 BCE.

Sybaris, founded by Achaean Greeks in the late 8th century BCE during Greek colonisation, had grown very rich from farmland and trade. Stories of its luxury became famous: Sybarites were said to ban noisy trades from the city so they could sleep. A "sybarite" still means someone devoted to pleasure.

A political quarrel led to war. Croton's army was led by the wrestler Milo, six times an Olympic champion and a follower of Pythagoras. Croton won, and according to tradition it diverted the river Crathis over the ruins so nothing would remain.

Survivors tried to rebuild, and in 444 BCE Athens helped found the new city of Thurii nearby; Herodotus is said to have been among its settlers. The site of Sybaris was found by archaeologists in the 1960s.
sum: The destruction of Sybaris, a Greek city on the Gulf of Taranto in southern Italy, by its neighbour Croton in 510 BCE.
